subject: chemistry-1
question: Which set of coefficients, written in the order N2, H2, NH3, balances the equation N2 + H2 -> NH3 using the smallest whole numbers?
explanation:
With 1, 3, 2 the left side has 2 N and 6 H and the right side has 2 N and 6 H, so every element balances with the smallest possible whole numbers. Each other set fails an atom count: 1, 2, 2 gives 4 H on the left against 6 H on the right; 2, 3, 2 gives 4 N on the left against 2 N on the right; 1, 3, 3 gives 2 N on the left against 3 N on the right. Balancing is done only by adjusting coefficients, because changing a subscript would change the identity of a substance.

ELI-10: Count atoms on each side and adjust only the numbers written in front. One N2 supplies 2 nitrogen atoms, and each NH3 uses 1 nitrogen, so 2 NH3 can be built. Those 2 NH3 need 6 hydrogen atoms, and hydrogen arrives as H2 pairs, so 3 H2 are required. Final tally: 2 N and 6 H on both sides.
